> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/automation/:name (route, 40 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 185512ccaf6394364a0da1af55cd8f1bfae37869` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0f37e4d4c89bab8b62872b7265beb4c14528158f` — the merge of head `3fb9ba31997f8f7291aa85823ed313d1838c26b5` into base `185512ccaf6394364a0da1af55cd8f1bfae37869`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0f37e4d4c89bab8b62872b7265beb4c14528158f && git checkout 0f37e4d4c89bab8b62872b7265beb4c14528158f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 185512ccaf6394364a0da1af55cd8f1bfae37869 3fb9ba31997f8f7291aa85823ed313d1838c26b5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 185512ccaf6394364a0da1af55cd8f1bfae37869 && git merge --no-ff 3fb9ba31997f8f7291aa85823ed313d1838c26b5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 185512ccaf6394364a0da1af55cd8f1bfae37869
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 185512ccaf6394364a0da1af55cd8f1bfae37869` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3fb9ba31997f8f7291aa85823ed313d1838c26b5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/deleted-flow-decision-refusal.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/unresumable-suspension-cause.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approvals-plugin.ts (the production attach site), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-node.ts (`ApprovalAutomationSurface`), packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts (`registerService('automation', this.engine)`), packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts (the entry that publishes `AutomationEngine`), packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts (the 409/500 wire map), packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts and packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts (the published `RESUME_TARGET_LOST` text; untouched), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-engine-double-contract.mjs (the readers of the declaration lines and of the ledger). The prose face `.changeset/26477-decision-on-deleted-flow-refused.md` is read for ②.

Inputs read: card #26477 body and all three comments (triage `6434168375`, claim `6434774168`, os-dev-report `6436133857`); PR #26544 body, file list (7 files) and `git diff origin/main...3fb9ba3199` (merge base `45de8c6cba`); the head's check-runs at 2026-10-27T07:24Z and again at 2026-10-27T07:29Z. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the Clause-② line was graded against the regex in `clause2-line.mjs` by reading, not by executing it.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, in the cited code at the head:

1. **Accept-set narrowing — the decision doors.** `assertRunResumable` (approval-service.ts:4587) now asks `unresumableSuspensionCause(runId)` after `hasSuspendedRun` answers `true`, and throws `RESUME_TARGET_LOST: … can never be resumed: CAUSE …` before the first write. It is called at :4387 inside `decideNode` (the shared path of `decide` → `decideAndResume` → `decideNode`, so approve AND reject, finalizing and non-finalizing votes alike), :5405 (`sendBack`) and :5579 (`resubmit`). `recall` (:5025) does NOT call it, which is what makes the remedy the refusal names ("recall the request") reachable: the recall's resume settles the orphan (#23963), and the fifth approvals pin proves it. `reassign` (:5694) resumes nothing and needs no pre-flight. Before the diff the same calls wrote the decision row, flipped the request, and answered 500 `RESUME_FAILED` with `finalized: true`; after it they answer 409 with nothing written. **Right**: this is door (b) of triage `6434168375` exactly ("the decision path refuses before it records"), and it is a narrowing of a published accept set, so the `(narrowing)` arm is owed and declared.
2. **The refusal is the existing code, not a new one.** `RESUME_TARGET_LOST` is already in `error-code-ledger.zod.ts:277` and mapped to 409 by `approvals-routes.ts:126` from the message prefix; the throw is the same plain-`Error`-with-prefix shape the #4420 pre-flight uses (:4606). No new error code, so execution-duties line 109 (a new code is always `yes` and must be registered) is not triggered. **Right.**
3. **One classification, not two.** `resolveResumeTarget` (run-resume.ts) is the two never-dispatched exits of `resumeInternal` lifted verbatim: the cause strings are byte-identical to the deleted lines, `resumeInternal` consumes it at the same point (after `loadSuspendedRunStrict`, before `creditChildRun`), and the resume's ordering, `RESUME_IN_PROGRESS` guard, `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` branch and `settleUnresumableSuspension` are untouched. The engine's probe and the resume both load through `loadSuspendedRunStrict`, so an outage rejects in both (the #4420 posture `hasSuspendedRun` already has). `unresumable-suspension-cause.test.ts` pins cause == resume `error` for both causes. **Right**: the resume behaviour from #23963 is not moved.
4. **Pre-seal behaviour.** Before `sealNodeTypeVocabulary` the probe answers `Flow 'F' not found …` without settling; the resume on the same state returns the `RUN_NOT_FOUND` refusal without settling either (`settleUnresumableSuspension`: `if (!this.nodeTypeVocabularySealed) return refusal`). So a decision that somehow reached the door mid-boot is refused 409 and nothing is recorded that a later registration would have to undo — AGENTS.md "Startup registry reads" part 3 (a recorded verdict) is absent; a read-only probe is legal by that section's own words. The approvals plugin seals at `kernel:bootstrapped` and attaches at the same `init`, so in a live server the window is nominal. **Right.**
5. **Public-surface widening.** `AutomationEngine` is re-exported from `service-automation/src/index.ts:4`, so the new public `async unresumableSuspensionCause(runId)` (resolving to a cause string or `undefined`) is reachable from the package entry and enlarges the public surface — execution-duties line 67's second criterion, hence `Clause-②: yes`. `resolveResumeTarget` is exported from `run-resume.ts` but `index.ts` does not re-export `run-resume`, so it is NOT published. `ApprovalResumeSurface.unresumableSuspensionCause?` is an optional member on a plugin-internal interface; the production attach (`approvals-plugin.ts:594`) hands the real engine registered at `service-automation/src/plugin.ts:968`, so the member is present at runtime and the fix is live in a stock stack, not only in the test's wiring. An engine double without it degrades to the #4420 check alone, as the docblock says. **Right, and correctly declared as `widened:`.**
6. **Fail-open posture.** A probe that rejects falls into the existing `catch`, warns, and returns — the decision proceeds and the post-resume `RESUME_FAILED` report still catches a real failure. This is the posture `hasSuspendedRun` already had; the fourth approvals pin holds it. It is a deliberate tolerance, not a widening (the accept set under an outage is unchanged from before the diff). **Right.**
7. **Residual race.** Check-then-write is ordered, not atomic: a flow deleted between the pre-flight and the resume still lands on the post-resume `RESUME_FAILED` with the decision recorded. The PR names it, it is the #4420 window unchanged in width, and the card's "never answer a 500 after committing the decision" is satisfied for the reproduced sequence (delete, then decide). **Right as a disclosed residual, not a defect of this diff.**
8. **Door (a) not added.** The claim allowed `packages/runtime/**` "only if door (a) is added"; the diff touches no runtime path and the PR says so. `DELETE /automation/:name` still drops a flow with paused runs silently — recorded by the dev as an out-of-scope finding, carrier none. **Right** against the claim; see ③ for the follow-up.
9. **Ledger row.** `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains the two rows (`delete`, `update`, pinned 1) for the new approvals test, written by the gate's own `--write` (`SEAM_REGEN` in `check-engine-double-contract.mjs:2450`, the sanctioned path: "then commit"). The test's fake is the `decision-strand-envelope.test.ts` double copied whole, routing writes through `assertEngineUpdateDispatch`/`assertEngineDeleteDispatch`. `check:engine-double-contract` and `check:objectql-double-limit` are in the dev's 72-run sheet at exit 0 and "Lint · CI, release & engine gates" is `success` on the head. **Right.**
10. **No spec, no governed path.** `packages/spec/**` is untouched (lane red line honoured); the Governed Surface Queue Guard and the single-writer-path check are both `success` on the head.

Nothing in the diff widens an accept set. The only enlargement is item 5.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/26477-decision-on-deleted-flow-refused.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-approvals: patch`, `@objectstack/service-automation: patch` — the two packages the diff moves, and only those (`scripts/` and the test files publish nothing). `rest` and `spec` are not moved and correctly carry no entry.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing an author writes against is added, narrowed or re-meant; the change is a runtime refusal. Under maintainer ruling A (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist ③; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` verdict table, `none-clean`) the level follows the kind alone, so `none` ⇒ `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". **`patch` is the ruled level**; `minor` would be wrong here despite the `!`.
- BREAKING carriers all present and consistent: the `!` on the `fix(plugin-approvals)!:` summary (and the PR title), the `**BREAKING**` banner with Before / Now / Fix, and the `(narrowing)` arm. `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` collects those three signals and demands a disposition; the body carries `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) …`, which parses under the gate's `not-required (category …) why` grammar. The category is honest: no authorable key, export or config field is renamed or removed, so there is no FROM → TO mapping to register. "Check Changeset" and "Lint · PM dispatch-gates" are `success` on the head.
- `Clause-②:` line, identical on the PR body and the changeset, line-initial on both: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing: …; widened: …)`. Read against `readClause2Line`: value `yes`; the arm regex `^\([ \t]*(widening|narrowing)(?![A-Za-z0-9_])(?![ \t]*\|)` matches `(narrowing:` because the colon is neither a word character nor a pipe, so the arm reads `narrowing`, not malformed; `yes (narrowing)` is the narrowing face by the recogniser's own battery ("a diff that widens and narrows owes the narrowing review"). The declaration matches what the diff publishes — item ① 1 is the narrowing, item ① 5 the widening. The prose inside the parenthesis names approve, reject and send-back but not resubmit; the changeset's bullet and the code do include resubmit. Cosmetic: the arm, not the prose, is what the gates read, and the narrowing it declares covers all four doors.
- Both line-initial declarations also appear in the PR body as the template requires.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions[0]` — Clause-② `no` (claim) vs `yes (narrowing …; widened …)` (measured): answered, option A, the line as shipped is right.** The claim's `no` was written before the diff existed and reserved the measurement to the dev ("The dev measures it on the diff"). Measured: the diff narrows a published accept set (arm `narrowing`) AND adds a public method on a published class (`yes`). Execution-duties line 106 makes a pure narrowing `no (narrowing)`; the widening in ① 5 lifts it to `yes`, and lanes/spec.md line 21 says declaring `yes` is never an error. The arm is what makes the ADR-0087 gate ask for a disposition, as the dev says. No rewrite of body or changeset is owed. The seat should note the claim-vs-measured delta in its ACCEPT rather than ask for a `no`.
- **Dev flag: dogfood battery pinned to `bd15ba3d1`, not the head `3fb9ba3199` — escalated to the seat.** review-checklist.md line 50 wants the battery pinned to the head for a `!`/`(narrowing)` PR. `git diff --stat bd15ba3d1 3fb9ba3199` is exactly the two files the dev names: `deleted-flow-decision-refusal.test.ts` (+49/−12) and `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` (+10). `@objectstack/dogfood` lives at `packages/qa/dogfood` and does not collect another package's vitest files or read the gate ledger, so the battery's inputs did not move; the CI "Dogfood Regression Gate" is `success` on the head itself. Materially the pin holds; whether the letter of the checklist is satisfied by that argument is the seat's enqueue call, not a contract defect.
- **Residual race (dev-flagged, ① 7):** disclosed, unchanged in width from #4420, pinned by `approval-restart-resume.test.ts` per the PR. No decision owed.
- **Door (a) not filed (dev out-of-scope finding, carrier none):** `DELETE /api/v1/automation/:name` and an uninstall still remove a flow with paused runs without naming them. After this PR no decision is recorded against such a run, so the user-visible wrong answer the card reported is gone; the orphan row still reads `paused` until something resumes it (recall settles it). The triage ruling asked for ONE honest door, so (a) is not owed by this card, but the silent delete is a legitimate follow-up for the automation domain. Escalated to the seat as a candidate card, not a condition on this PR.
- **Published contract text now under-describes the 409 (my flag, not the dev's):** `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts:701` says `RESUME_TARGET_LOST` is "when the run behind the request no longer exists"; after this PR it is also "exists but can never be dispatched". The lane red line forbids a spec edit on this card and the ledger comment at `error-code-ledger.zod.ts:277` reads the same way. The code's own message says "can never be resumed … the flow was deleted or edited while the run was paused", so the wire body is honest. Follow-up docblock touch for the spec lane; no condition on this PR.
- **Same-family residual outside the decision doors (my note):** `continueRestoredRun` (approval-service.ts:7092, #15389) still pre-flights with `hasSuspendedRun` alone. It is a restore-then-continue path, not a decision door, and nothing in the card or the ruling covers it; noted for the seat, no action owed here.
- **Refusal pins assert the thrown message prefix, not an envelope `code`/`status`:** the service throws a prefixed `Error`, as the #4420 pre-flight does, and the status is stamped at the REST door (pinned in `rest-approvals-wire-codes.test.ts`). The ADR-0112 check in review-checklist.md applies to the lane seat's ACCEPT; from the contract side the code is the prefix and the mapping is unchanged, so nothing is owed.
- **Open PR #26337** edits `approval-service.ts` in other hunks; the dev reports a clean local `merge-tree`. The single-writer-path check is `success`. Serial-order of the two merges stays with the seat.

Check-runs on `3fb9ba3199`, read three times, last at 2026-10-27T07:31Z: 44 runs; every completed required family is `success` — Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, all Type Check and Lint sub-jobs, Build Core, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, both single-claim guards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test Core shards 2/3/6/7/8; UI, docs, Temporal and opt-in families `skipped` by the path filter. Still `in_progress` at review time: Test Core (1/8), (4/8), (5/8). No failure or cancellation on the head. The seat re-reads those three shards before enqueue; this verdict does not pre-empt them.
